title: Use an icon array to make a share countable as people out of 100.
rule: Draw 100 plain unit marks in rows of 10, read from the top left, and fill one in the subject ink for each person the share counts; leave the rest open, with a thin edge in the context ink and no fill. Round the share to whole people and print the published figure in the table. Draw one share, and give a comparison the publisher qualifies, such as another year, in a note. A Civic Line drawing may head the chart once, at 48 px beside the name and typed chip chapter 10 gives it, as the chart’s subject and outside the grid; the marks stay plain squares (Rules 10.1, 10.4 and 10.6).
use_when: The reader asks how many of every 100 people something touches, and one share answers it, such as the one worker in ten who belonged to a union in 2025.

use_instead.when: The reader compares shares across groups or years
Each mark is a record the reader can trace, such as one entry in a log
One figure answers the question by itself

text: A reader counts 10 filled squares in a row of 10 faster than they can turn 10.0 percent into people, and a grid of 100 makes one in ten something to see. Filled against open holds in gray print and for a reader who sees no color. A symbol drawn in each square would give a Civic Line drawing a second meaning, one person, so the squares stay plain.
why.basis: Design judgment, from the chart system our founder and editor approved in November 2026

builders: Form icon-array: node work/build/chart-kit/oa-chart.mjs build s85; labels.draw picks the row the array draws, labels.filled and labels.open set the key’s words, and labels.topic sets the Civic Line drawing, its name and its chip.
